messages:
Alex (support): Heads up — customer 'Findry' opened an urgent ticket. Their embedding pipeline started failing after a weekend deploy. Hosted API returns 1536-dimensional embeddings, but Dedicated nodes are returning 1024 dims. This causes downstream index mismatch and 500s on their side. They say it started ~Sat 02:00 UTC.

Priya (ml-eng): Ugh. do we know which model variant they're calling? hosted/dedicated should be identical model configs.

Alex (support): They said model param = "open-embed-1" and the call is the standard embeddings endpoint. Key used: customer-key-*** (we masked). They repro with a single curl call:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-findry-xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":"test string"}' | jq .data[0].embedding | length
```

On Hosted this returns 1536, on Dedicated it returns 1024. They also tried private deploy and got 1536.

Ethan (infra): Any chance of a routing mismatch to a legacy quantized variant? We recently added a compatibility alias for older nodes.

Priya (ml-eng): Possible. There's a new quantization profile rolled last Friday that changes the exported topology, and we have an alias map: open-embed-1 -> [open-embed-1-fp16, open-embed-1-quant]. Normally runtime normalizes dims but looks like when serving from the quantized path we lost a projection head.

Jamie (support): Customer sent logs showing response shape header: `{"embedding_dim":1024}` from dedicated endpoint. Hosted responses show `{"embedding_dim":1536}`. They included a repro script that toggles `batching=true/false` and sees dims flip only when batch size > 1 on Dedicated.

Priya (ml-eng): That is key — batching interacting with backend variant selection. If a request is batched across different serving partitions, the router might pick a different cached model instance. Need to check model variant mapping at the router level.

Ethan (infra): I can grep routing logs for that customer key and timeframe. ops-bot, can you pull last 48h routing decisions for model=open-embed-1 and customer=Findry?

ops-bot: Query queued. Returning aggregated routing table (truncated):
- route shard-a: open-embed-1-fp16 (1536) -> served 62%
- route shard-b: open-embed-1-quant (1024) -> served 38%
- note: dedicated pool DC-west has higher % of quant variant usage last 24h

Priya (ml-eng): That matches suspicion — Dedicated DC-west seems to prefer quant variant to save memory. But the quant variant should produce same dim (shouldn't drop projection). Looks like the export for quant variant accidentally used an older model checkpoint without the final projection layer. If batching causes cross-shard pool selection, mixed dims will appear in a single batch but runtime should reject or pad, which it's not.

Oncall (sre): This can cause consumer errors and index corruption. Two things to do now: 1) immediate mitigation: pin customer to hosted routing or to the correct variant; 2) root-cause: find how quant export lost the projection and why runtime didn't validate dim invariants.

Ethan (infra): I added a temporary routing rule to force Findry's API key to hosted pool for embeddings (rule id tmp-1892). Propagating now. Will notify when effective.

ops-bot: Routing rule tmp-1892 applied to key sk-findry-xxx. TTL 6h.

Jamie (support): Customer confirmed they see consistent 1536 once routed to hosted. They still want a durable fix — they asked for explanation and ETA.

Priya (ml-eng): For root cause: I'll check the model build CI. My hypothesis: quant export job (job id: export-2026-03-06-q) used checkpoint v12 which predates projection layer v13. The build pipeline should have a dim check but it was recently silenced during refactor. I'll re-run export with v14 checkpoint and push new quant artifact.

Ethan (infra): Also raising a runtime validation alert: runtime should assert embedding dim equals model manifest. SRE, recommend we add a hard reject for mismatched embedding length in batch responses and a metric for "embedding_dim_mismatch".

Oncall (sre): Agreed. Creating incident CH-embed-1892 to track. Immediate SLA impact: moderate.

Jamie (support): Customer asked about billing — they got charged for failed indexing jobs. Can we issue credit for the window where we served mismatched dims? I put a billing ticket.

Ethan (infra): Create a script to scan logs for requests served by open-embed-1-quant that returned 1024 dims between 2026-03-06T00:00Z and 2026-03-08T00:00Z. We'll use that to scope credits.

Priya (ml-eng): Action items I'm taking:
- re-run quant export with correct checkpoint and verify dim = 1536 locally (repro script attached)
- add unit test in model-export CI to assert final projection present
- coordinate with infra to retire bad artifact

Ethan (infra): My actions:
- rollback alias for quant variant for dedicated pool until we confirm fix
- add runtime dim-check and a small patch to reject mixed-dim batches (hotfix)
- produce routing audit for affected keys

Jamie (support): I'll keep Findry updated and request usage timeline + ask for any additional repros.

Alex (support): Summary for ticket: temporary fix = pin to hosted; eta for durable fix = Priya will validate new quant artifact today and infra will deploy hotfix deploy by EOD; billing credit scoped after log scan. Customer OK with temporary routing but wants a postmortem.

Priya (ml-eng): I'll open a PR for export CI checks + new artifact and ping this thread with links.

Oncall (sre): Keep me looped for postmortem. Also schedule a follow-up 24h after hotfix to ensure metrics normal.

Jamie (support): Noting follow-up items in the ticket. Thanks team :thumbsup:

Alex (support): Closing loop here — hosted routing mitigation held. Will reopen if dims reappear.
